findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive, allowing trivial bypass
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up records with `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` using the exact string passed in. User emails are matched case-insensitively elsewhere in the app (e.g. Email.downcase is used in UsersController#change_email), but a blocked entry for 'spammer@evil.com' will not match a signup with 'Spammer@Evil.com' or 'SPAMMER@evil.com', so anyone can bypass the block list just by changing letter case. The email should be normalized (downcased) both when the BlockedEmail record is created and when it is looked up.

findings.title: should_block? performs a database write inside a validation
findings.body: should_block? is called from EmailValidator#validate_each, which runs during user.valid? — i.e. on every signup attempt and every form retry — and it increments match_count and saves the BlockedEmail record each time. This has two problems: (1) a validation method should be side-effect free; the counter save happens even if the surrounding user save later rolls back, and any validation failure on the BlockedEmail record itself would silently fail to save, and (2) every failed signup attempt triggers an extra UPDATE query. The statistics update should be moved out of the validator (e.g. only recorded on actual blocked signup attempts in the controller), or done with update_counters to avoid running the record's full validations.

findings.title: Domain restriction regex is not anchored at the end, so whitelist/blacklist can be evaded or misapplied
findings.body: email_in_restriction_setting? builds the pattern `@(domains)` with no end anchor. With a whitelist of 'mycompany.com', an address like 'attacker@mycompany.com.evil.org' matches and is accepted; conversely a blacklisted domain matches any address whose domain merely starts with it. The regex should be anchored (e.g. `@(#{domains})$` or matching against the parsed domain) so the comparison is against the actual email domain.

findings.title: Uniqueness validation plus unique index has a race with no exception handling
findings.body: BlockedEmail validates uniqueness of email and the migration adds a unique index, but two concurrent inserts of the same email can both pass validation, and the second will raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique/StatementInvalid on save. Nothing rescues this, so any code path or admin console creating blocked emails concurrently will surface a 500. Either handle the exception or rely on the index with an upsert.
